Messages.Author: js_vtes
Messages.Body:
A Black Cat/Beretta deck based on ideas from  this discussion .

I tried building an Anarch version with Undue Influence, but all the Anarch tech fattened up the deck and got in the way of the trick, i.e.: Black Cat gets a metric butt-tonne of Berettas and Nods them to her pals. So I switched to weenie CEL.

Any suggestions for improvement would be welcome, particularly ways to cut the deck size. 16 Beretta/16 Concealed Weapon in 80 cards almost works, but if I could cut the deck to 70 (or smaller?), it would probably work way better. But what to drop? There are lots of permanents in there. I might like to try to find room for a Dragon's Breath Rounds or two, maybe some Taste of VItae.

How do you intend to oust?
Several bleeds for 2 or 3 per turn.

How do you intend to keep from being ousted?
Tributes, permanent intercept, back-rushing.

What do you want your ready region to look like?
Black Cat and three or more well-armed assistants.

What do you want your average turn to look like?
Early game: Black Cat picks a fight (bleeding, rushing or blocking) and loads up on Berettas. After she's passed them around to her friends, it's just a matter of keeping the pressure on.

What's your metagame like? How do your opponents play?
All kinds of stuff. People here seem to like to spend time tooling up before throwing down.

What problems have you observed with the deck in play?
No Black Cat in the opening crypt sucks. The trick is also dependent on a good draw. One game, my opening hand had a couple Berettas/CW, and I just kept top-decking more, so Black Cat had lots of guns to pass around when Nod came up (which it did right away). The game before, though: no guns for the first dozen or so cards. Hence the desire to trim the deck size.

Thanks in advance!

Messages.Author: direwolf
Messages.Body:
I've tried berettas. I want to like them. Really I do. Even if you can get them for free, they take up card space (and the concealed weapon to go with it!)

Try adding another Black Cat. 5 copies in a 13 vampire crypt is ideal.

Consider using .44 Magnums. You can cut 16 cards (8 guns and 8 concealeds) at the cost of paying 1 pool for each. (if your deck is 90 cards, be lucky if you see 4 of them anyway.)

You could also consider using a mix of Saturday Night Specials and .44s and including Suppressing Fire.

Independent Futurist. Contrarian (titled, X votes where X is the number of votes as the acting minion.) Target Vitals is always the better combat card.

Messages.Author: Azel
Messages.Body:
Why do people lynch pin this to Black Cat, besides the obvious pool savings? It complicates things. Throw in Jack of Both Sides so your other minions can discount the guns. That should speed up things considerably.

Naturally Pier 13, Leather Jacket, Concealed, etc. stays in.

Now what you do about ousting... that's on you. A lone copy of Fame and two unique bleed retainers equals a whole lot of bleeds for one. How do you want to shape the crypt to improve this? Brujah w/ Legal/Public? Flurry of Action to bleed for one and stay up?

Suppressing Fire or Resist Earth's Grasp seem generally useful here, at the very least letting your rush land on your target.

I don't know what you want to do about defense. You look like the bleed sink here. Dodd & Anvil for Deflections? Major Boon and or Dummy Corp with Aversions and or Keep it Simple? Gotta make a decision. Four Tributes with midcaps is just not enough bloat for defense, IME.

Messages.Author: js_vtes
Messages.Body:
Thanks to everyone for the thought-provoking comments and suggestions!

I'm going to stick with the Berettas rather than the more "reliable" .44s. I would still need to pack the deck with them to draw them reliably, and every pool I spend on one is a pool I can't use to bring out another guy to pass along a bunch of FREE guns to. Four .44s mean no Victor or Jimmy. As Mr. Bajika put it in the linked discussion above:

> Non-existant user wrote:
> ...it isn't a *good* deck, but it has a plan, and that plan is "Black Cat gets a million Berettas for free and spreads them around with Nod." If Black Cat is getting a million .44s, they aren't free, and you just oust yourself...
>
So yes, this deck's more for fun than a tier-one tournament-blaster. But it did do some things surprisingly well:

- A minion with 3 Berettas can press twice and gets a free maneuver ALL THREE rounds. A .44 would just give you one.
- 3 Berettas + 2 Ghoul Retainers = 6R damage, before any additional strikes. Press, everybody passes their guns around and does it again. Ouch.
- Minion A has a Laptop and J.S. Simmons. That's a 3-point bleed. Heidelberg that stuff to Minion B and repeat. Then there's Minion C who's been sitting there with Tasha, too. Point is, it can do much more than just lots of bleeds for 1.

> Dr.Mafrune wrote:
> This is clearly another deck where you would greatly benefit from abusing from recursive combo infernal pursuit + ashur tablets.
>
> First part fetch near to all guns to black cat and deplete your deck.
> Second part play nod and get all celerity and rushes back to the deck.
> Third part is action time.
>
YES!! LOVE it! (Of course, I would expect nothing but good advice from a doctor.) The seed of the deck idea is that, after "the plan" has been pulled off, I'm left with a 40-or-so-card deck that I would move through pretty quickly, slapping permanents into play and drawing into the transient stuff just often enough. I was considering an Ashur module, but Infernal Pursuit is EXACTLY the missing element I need to make it swing.

And those bad boys stack, too, don't they? So if I play one each time I draw it, I could very well burn through my whole deck during that first combat. I just have to be smart enough (a shaky proposition at best) to leave myself with a decent hand when the dust settles. Say, Parthenon, Ashur, Ashur, Ashur, Nod...? Any other suggestions?

> Suoli wrote:
> Fourth part: realize Black Cat is spelled Anson.
>
Hmm. I thought he might just be too big for the deck's premise, but he'd certainly come in handy for the whole "burn through cards fast" plan. Nothing like chiseling out 3 Ashur Tablets in one shot.

Thanks again, all! Any more thoughts, please share!

Messages.Author: Dr.Mafrune
Messages.Body:
The combo of berettas with ghoul retainer is pretty interesting, but there are two problems that arise from its inclusion in the deck:

1) It costs two pool, not blood; which is the typical tool-up cost you wanted to avoid making this deck. If the focus of the deck is to spare pool, I wouldn´t spend it if not absolutely necesary. On the other side, the pool cushion you have is the only defense you have against bleeds; therefore I think is quite wise to preserve it.

2) You have to invest a valuable action to equip it. For a deck which has only american defense, every action has a high opportunity cost.
The kind of decission you have to face is whether to have a nice ghoul and a "friendly Mr.Chains" blowing on your nape one turn more or try to let him have a peaceful existence....in torpor this turn. On pure rush decks free lunch actions are very, very scarce.
